column8: Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 answer to the devil's advocate, or store: finished books' royalties do sell, at about 5.5 years' income (Head First series, 20 Dec 2021; 1.43% checked in the repo's DGS10 file); can't sell holds for work not yet done; never set the 18.3% first-year yield against the Treasury as like for like (it includes decay), and never as a hint that Laura sell anything.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 1 (a finished stream sold at about five years' income; 5.3x and 2.61% check); a trademark licence on a curriculum, so the link to Laura's books read in classrooms is a stretch; store only.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; a publisher's subscription share, far from an author; check '2.9 times the 3-year average' against the listing: the listed 2023-2025 earnings average $33,137, which gives 3.3 times (Keel arithmetic); 4.97x and -51% check.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of row 1 (one finished stream sold near 6 times a year's income); the marketplace's own promotional blog and one seller; its fund-a-venture angle reads as the advice the card itself rules out, so store only.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; marketing claims read as claims; never 'about 8 points over Treasuries' (an all-years average yield on decaying streams set against one day's 10-year, 24 Sep 2026) and never 'because they are not guaranteed' (decay and illiquidity sit in that spread); 'uncorrelated' is the seller's word, answered by Q96-021 and Q96-028.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or the one figure behind 2.3's answer to 'royalties trade': across 2,683 deals a finished stream sold at a median 6.1 times last year's income, streams under five years old at 4.6; mostly music, unadjusted medians, a third party's compilation; say they fetch the lowest multiple, never 'cheapest to sell'.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or a 3e clause only if a judge asks about the backlist; 52% is about half, never 'usually sold on the way down'; streams decay anyway (median -1.7% a year), so 74% below peak is not a seller's timing; drop 'the moment a creator most needs to sell' (selection is measured, not timing).

Wed 18 Nov: refuse as stated: its own dates contradict the rate reading, since dated deals fell from 200 (2019) to 38 (2021) while the 10-year sat near record lows (1.43% on 20 Dec 2021, row 1), and only 884 of 2,552 records carry dates, so the fall may be a data gap; the stable 4.7x-6.4x medians can live in row 6's note.

Wed 18 Nov: store only: in 2022-23 owners held royalty assets back rather than sell cheap (Edison on Round Hill, a fund's research note, music); the seller's-side companion to Q96-028; no part needs it.
Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q96-028 (private catalogue multiples drifted down as rates rose); adds only 2024's recorded-music 13x against 13.8x, read through Billboard, not Shot Tower's report; store only.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 or 3d clause at most: the Bowie bonds' credit support came from EMI, which weakened in the same slump, as a co-sponsor's budget can fall in the same downturn as her income (can, never together); adds the guarantor to Q96-031; EMI's role rests on the Guardian, Moody's own notice unread.

Wed 18 Nov: a writers' guard, store only: if the Bowie bonds are cited, Baa3 (one notch above junk, the 2004 cut), never CNBC's BBB+, the equal of Baa1; the scale mapping is standard but Keel's reading here.

Wed 18 Nov: store: a way to sell a creator's past work can dry up with the industry's own cycle (1997-2004); say 'dried up for years', never 'shut', since Q96-027 shows a 2024 royalty bond; music only.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or 2.3 evidence beside row 1: a song catalogue's royalty claim has traded since 1964 (EDGAR 10-Ks read); a publisher's catalogue, not an author's own royalties, so row 1 is the closer case; unit prices not found.

Wed 18 Nov: store, beside Q96-003 and Q96-042 (the backlist is the bond-like part): Mills's receipts fell 12.8% in 2008 against shares' 36.55%, but 26.4% over 2005-08 before the crash (Keel arithmetic checks); never name CDs as the cause unless the 10-K does; receipts lag a year.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or a 2.1 contrast clause: a royalty's payout passes through a payer's accounting and can be fought over (Mills's costs took 58% of 2025 receipts amid a dispute with EMI; checks), while a Treasury's coupon is fixed by contract; this trust's costs are its own, never typical.

Wed 18 Nov: store only: about 6% of a 1964 catalogue's titles earn (the filings' title counts conflict, 25,000 against over 12,000); the leap to one author's backlist is weak, since Laura's few books are not a catalogue.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or the legal footnote to 2.3's can't sell: US law voids service compelled to work off a debt (1867); 'her future labour cannot be pledged' overreaches, since income can be promised (row 26, the ISAs), so say the work itself cannot be compelled; US law only, Laura's jurisdiction is not in the case; mind the register beside a client.

Wed 18 Nov: store or a 2.3 clause: a promise of personal service is never specifically enforced, so a buyer of her future work gets damages at most, never the work (Restatement 367, read on Open Casebook's copy).

Wed 18 Nov: store only; California's seven-year cap binds employees, and authors are rarely employees; drop 'the plan runs to 2042, longer than any such bond': a plan's horizon and a service contract's cap are unrelated.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3, one clause at most (the card's best): bankruptcy law splits a debtor's finished work (its royalties go to creditors) from earnings for later services (11 U.S.C. 541(a)(6), read); fix 'the deposit comes from the second kind': the case's advances and speaking are work still to be done, but licensing can rest on finished books (Q96-040's note), so say 'mostly'; Cusano unread; never put Laura near a bankruptcy.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; 17 U.S.C. 201(e) bars a government or official body from seizing an individual author's copyright, and its House report counts bankruptcy and mortgages as consent, so never 'outside bankruptcy no one can force a sale'; it adds nothing a part needs.
Wed 18 Nov: store, or 2.3's middle tier with row 24: an advance sells one future book's rights, never the career (UK CDPA s.91 read; US practice differs; Taiwan not searched).

Wed 18 Nov: store: the nearest thing to selling a creator's next work is a short first look (Authors Guild model, 60 days); the Dickens price is from the Society of Authors' page, so keep it as theirs.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 reference candidate: Friedman (1955), the investing literature's own source for can't sell, and why even a legal sale would not be a bond (the asset needs its owner's co-operation); quote the second sentence, not the slavery clause, beside a client.

Wed 18 Nov: store, the other half of row 25: the law forbids selling the person, not a slice of income; costs (Friedman) and adverse selection (row 29) kept the market small; keep 'partial slavery' out of report prose.

Wed 18 Nov: store; never 'the only legal way to sell a career's future income is to borrow against it': Fantex sold registered shares in brand income (rows 30-32) and Friedman saw no legal obstacle (row 26); say US regulators treat income share agreements as credit (CFPB 2021, education finance), and drop 'a borrower carries the risk' (payments are income-contingent).
Wed 18 Nov: store only: Purdue's income share programme ran 2016-22 and paused after the CFPB order and its servicer's exit; students, not creators.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 support or store: the economic reason a career cannot be sold is adverse selection (Herbst and Hendren 2024, AER); read the paper itself before it enters References (summary only so far).

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3, one clause with rows 31-32: the only firm found to float shares in people's careers postponed its first IPO after the player's back surgery (12 Nov 2013, sources read); drop 'which is what the IPS means': IPS l.9's stock is income that falls with the economy, an injury is risk in the person; athletes, not authors.

Wed 18 Nov: store, with row 30: one career slice did float (10% of a tight end's brand income, 421,100 shares at $10, 28 Apr 2014), sold once by a firm that took the risk; it is the tier that can be sold, so it supports row 40's split.

Wed 18 Nov: store or row 30's clause: Fantex's insiders bought 52% of its last offering (Keel arithmetic checks, 3,108,658 of 5,933,658 units) and it deregistered on 27 Jan 2017; drop 'almost no one outside the firm would buy it' (outsiders took 48%, 160 holders); say its own insiders bought about half.

Wed 18 Nov: store only; the 2021 award's grounds are unread (said second-hand to be California's athlete-agent law), so never 'claims on a person's future are fragile in law' until they are read; one player's arbitration.

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3 support for CANON A2: no market pays out when authors' income falls (Shiller's livelihood insurance was a proposal; 'no such market existed'), so the pitch's 'hedge' (quoted as the IPS's, CANON A1) is carried by l.9's counterbalance; never 'hedge' in Keel's own words (SKELETON 2.3); 'none exists' only as of the sources' dates.
Wed 18 Nov: References candidate for 2.3: the finance word is non-marketable assets (Mayers 1976, abstract read; Karolyi 2015, read); cite only what was read, never Mayers (1972) unread.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q1b-002 and Q39-001 (the average career is bond-like, the textbook objection SKELETON already answers); adds Fama and Schwert (1977); answered by the case's deposit sources (Q96-040), never a change to l.3.

Wed 18 Nov: twin of Q1b-002 (human capital mostly bond-like; Laura's deposit sources are the exception); the 93% is a model's figure read through Karolyi, paper unread; never set it beside the World Bank's 64%.

Wed 18 Nov: store, or 2.3 if room: human capital was 64% of measured world wealth in 2018 (World Bank 2021); its 'income groups' are groups of countries, so never 'for most people the career is about two-thirds of what they own'; 2.3 already has its one number (about three-quarters smaller).

Wed 18 Nov: 3e area (2) or 2.3: figures match NUMBERS as re-sized Tue 17 Nov evening (73.9%, $57,455, 99.965%; IPS l.17); the new line is that the plan relies on her career once, at a known date and size, never 'never relies on it'; the rest restates Q2a-024, Q2a-025 and the order-of-purchase reserve; say simulated futures, and keep 99.965% out of prose (no odds rarer than 1 in 100).

Wed 18 Nov: 2.3, one sentence if room: three tiers of sellability answer 'royalties trade' without weakening l.3; fix 'that is the part that pays the 2028 deposit' to 'most of what pays it' (licensing can rest on finished books, Q96-040), and 'every attempt closed' to 'the attempts found closed or were ruled credit' (new ones were tried in 2024 and 2026, the sources of rows 32-33); never beside Q96-042's bond-stock-option mapping.

Wed 18 Nov: store; drop 'missing buyers' (row 8 refused: the deal count fell before rates rose) and 'on the way down' (row 7: decay, not timing); what holds: institutional prices fell with rates (Q96 rows 14-29) and Mills's slide came before the 2008 crash; 3e has no room and the plan never counts a backlist.
